identity.title: Planetary Signatures in the SAO 206462 (HD 135344B) Disk: A Spiral Arm Passing through Vortex?

paper_type_evidence.quote: By carrying out two-dimensional, two-fluid hydrodynamic calculations, we find that a planetary-mass companion located at the outer disk could be responsible for these observed structures.

findings_qualitative.value: A spiral arm may pass through the vortex, boosting the scattered light, though the vortex alone may suffice

claims.hypothesis: A planet in the outer disk can produce spirals, asymmetric continuum and inner cavity in SAO 206462
claims.experiment: 2D two-fluid hydrodynamic simulations plus synthetic ALMA observations
claims.result: A 10-15 MJ planet at 100-120 au yields spirals, an inner-edge vortex and dust-depleted cavity resembling observations
claims.finding: A planetary companion could explain the observed structures

evidence.quote: We suggest that a planetary companion with a mass of 10–15 $M_J$ is orbiting SAO 206462 at 100–120 au.

claims.hypothesis: Spiral-vortex interaction explains the abrupt brightness change in the western arm
claims.experiment: Scenario with S1 as primary arm, 10 MJ at 100 au
claims.result: Primary arm passes through the inner-edge vortex
claims.finding: Plausible, but vortex alone may also explain it; 2D models cannot discriminate

evidence.quote: Our calculations are limited to two dimensions and, therefore, we are unable to conclude which scenario would be preferred over the other at this point.

why_this_method.value: Two-fluid calculations are needed to simulate dust as well as gas structures

evidence.quote: we perform two-fluid calculations where we can simulate dust as well as gas structures.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: S2 as primary arm requires 15 MJ at 120 au and no spiral-vortex boost

evidence.quote: a larger planetary mass of $M_p = 15~M_J$ is assumed so that the planet generates a stronger pressure bump at the gap edge.

limitations_admitted.value: 2D only; scattered light compared only qualitatively

evidence.quote: Thus, we compare the morphology of the arms and density distribution in a qualitative manner, rather than in a quantitative manner.
